standard.title: Experimenting with Linear Functions
standard.description: experiment with linear functions and relations using digital tools, making and testing conjectures and generalising emerging patterns
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can graph linear relations and describe relationships (from AC9M8A02, AC9M7A04, AC9M7A06). Students have used digital tools to vary parameters.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students systematically vary parameters of linear functions using digital tools, make and test conjectures, and generalise the effect of parameter changes on the graph.

nodes.label: Effect of gradient parameter on linear graphs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students investigate the effect of varying the gradient m in y = mx + b on the graph and generalise the relationship between m and steepness/direction.
nodes.minimum_width: Using graphing software, vary m across positive, negative and zero values; describe the effect on the graph.
nodes.typical_width: Systematically vary m; compare y = 2x and y = −2x; generalise the connection between the sign and magnitude of m and the graph's steepness and direction.
wider: Investigate what value of m produces a line perpendicular to a given line — discover the relationship m₁ × m₂ = −1 informally.
Explore the case m is undefined (vertical lines x = a) — why can't this be written as y = mx + b?

response_modes.reason: Making and testing conjectures requires an explicit investigation scaffold: vary one parameter, hold others constant, record observations, propose a general rule, test with a new case. Students who explore without structure draw weak or incorrect generalisations.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to vary both m and b systematically and generalise about parallel lines — students who have not acquired the conjecture-testing scaffold in Node 1 produce unfounded generalisations in Node 2 or confuse the effects of the two parameters.
success_criteria: Correctly describes the effect of varying m on the graph.
States a general rule for positive, negative and zero gradient.
Tests the conjecture with at least one new value.

nodes.label: Effect of intercept and generalising patterns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students investigate the effect of varying the y-intercept b, and generalise patterns including the behaviour of parallel lines.
nodes.minimum_width: Vary b in y = mx + b; describe the effect on the graph and state what b controls.
nodes.typical_width: Vary both m and b systematically; generalise that lines with the same m are parallel; investigate integer solutions to two-variable equations using digital tools.
wider: Investigate how linear functions are used in linear regression models in machine learning — describe what the gradient and intercept represent in this context.
Explore integer solutions to 2x + 3y = 48 — use digital tools to find all solutions and represent them on the Cartesian plane.

response_modes.reason: Generalising about linear functions requires encountering the pattern across multiple parameter combinations. Students who only investigate one direction miss the interaction between m and b.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Linear regression as a machine learning tool offers advancing students a genuine real-world connection — the gradient and intercept of a regression line have specific interpretable meanings that extend the Year 8 graphing work into data science.
success_criteria: Correctly states the effect of varying b on the graph.
Identifies that lines with equal gradient are parallel.
States a generalisation supported by evidence from their investigation.
